title: Always the Fixer? How to Stop Being the Team’s Emotional Dumping Ground
author: Colette Molteni
summary: Colette Molteni addresses the empathic team member who becomes the go-to venting outlet for colleagues, using a Slack-ping scenario with a coworker named Mason. Her central argument is that unlimited availability is not real empathy, because it keeps colleagues from building their own self-management. She draws on Goleman, Boyatzis and McKee's Primal Leadership to frame this person as an affiliative leader who heals rifts but risks being drained. Her move is to replace absorbing with reflecting: delay the response, then answer venting with curious questions that return the problem to the speaker. She closes with short recharge practices and the claim that self-management protects the capacity for empathy. The piece is a light, scenario-driven coaching post aimed at tech-sector professionals.
points: Constant availability to vent-prone colleagues can undermine their growth, since the empathic listener becomes a crutch rather than a developer of their self-management.
Delaying a reply is a legitimate tool, because by the time you respond the colleague's emotion has often passed and they have found their own route.
Reflecting with a curious question such as how would you approach it moves a looping colleague toward a constructive answer without dismissing them.
Brief daily practices like presence, a favorite song, and a ten-minute walk release absorbed emotional load and protect the leader's capacity for empathy.
quotes: You are an empathic person. You are not an emotionless AI. But is it really empathic if you never have them grow and learn their own self-management to make it through their challenges? If you are the crutch, how will they learn to run?

It’s okay to delay or acknowledge that response but not be available immediately. By the time you are available, their emotions will have most likely passed, and they will have had to figure out an alternate route rather than venting to you.

You can even reflect live and ask questions of curiosity, “How would you approach it?” Shift the conversation without ignoring it. You are listening but trying to move Mason out of his spiral constructively.
You lead with heart and give it your all. Work is not your whole life, but you give it your mind and soul while you are signed on.
You can delay the immediate gratification of a response to the Mason of your life. Sometimes, you don’t even have to respond at all. If you do, you do not have to absorb, but you can instead reflect.

Self-management will protect your peace and make you stronger. When you are stronger and feel at peace rather than being the betrodden dumping group, you maintain your capacity for empathy and become the successful you.
